summary: Tsinghua University in Beijing admits international students to master's and doctoral programmes through one online application. For 2027 entry, 54 schools and departments take applications, and 40 of their master's and doctoral programmes are taught in English. Scholarships are decided after admission: the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B, through Tsinghua's nomination), and tuition scholarships such as the Beijing Government Scholarship and the Tsinghua University Tuition Scholarship. Awards differ in what they cover, and none is automatic.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be foreign nationals with no Chinese nationality and a valid foreign passport or other valid proof of foreign nationality. Former Chinese citizens must have given up Chinese nationality, and at least six years must have passed since they acquired foreign nationality, counted to 30 April of the enrolment year. Applicants born abroad to Chinese-citizen parents must show that the parent or parents had permanent residence abroad by the applicant's birth. Nationality documents must reach Tsinghua by their stated deadline.

Master's applicants need a bachelor's degree or equivalent, and doctoral applicants a master's degree or equivalent. Thirty-nine schools and departments also accept bachelor's holders directly into doctoral study, with a normal study period of 4 to 5 years. Overseas degrees must be authenticated by CSCSE and Chinese mainland degrees recognised by the national system before registration, or admission is invalid. Students expected to graduate may apply and give the degree before registration.

Applicants must be in good health and conduct and follow Chinese law and university rules. Language (HSK for Chinese-taught, an English test for English-taught) and any work-experience conditions are set in each programme's remarks in the 2027 catalogue; someone who studied in Chinese may be exempted from HSK with a university certificate and school permission.

Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B) conditions: under 35 for master's and under 40 for doctoral applicants; HSK Level 4 for Chinese-taught programmes (not needed if the earlier degree was taught in Chinese at a Chinese university, with proof from that university); pre-admitted by Tsinghua and recommended by the school or department; not holding another scholarship for Tsinghua graduate study and not nominated by another Chinese university. Type B is not open to joint-degree programmes. Tuition scholarships such as the Beijing Government Scholarship have no age limit.
age_experience_notes: No age limit for admission is stated. For the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B) the age limit is under 35 (master's) and under 40 (doctoral). Tuition scholarships have no age limit. Some programmes list work-experience requirements in the 2027 catalogue.
funding_summary: A full Chinese Government Scholarship usually covers tuition, a free university dormitory or an accommodation subsidy, a stipend and comprehensive medical insurance; a partial award covers one or some of these. It lasts usually 1 to 3 academic years for master's students and 3 to 4 for doctoral students in the FAQ (the CGS page says master's 1 to 3 and doctoral 4 to 5 years), and the admission package states the exact period. Tuition scholarships (Beijing Government Scholarship, Tsinghua University Tuition Scholarship) cover full or partial tuition for one academic year and are applied for each year; the Beijing Government Scholarship usually also includes comprehensive medical insurance for that year. No stipend or subsidy amounts are stated.
programmes_note: Master's and doctoral programmes are offered across 54 schools and departments; 40 are taught in English and the rest in Chinese or bilingually. Most doctoral programmes in engineering and natural science are also conducted in English. Each department's programme list, language level, work-experience conditions and deadlines are in the 2027 Catalogue of Doctoral and Master's Programmes for International Students; the reminder notice says listings were being published on a rolling basis from early September to early October 2026. Applicants may name up to two programme preferences per cycle: the second opens only after the first is not admitted.
institutions_note: Single host university: Tsinghua University, with programmes at the Beijing campus and at the Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School. The Schwarzman Scholars Program and MBA programmes use separate application sites.

benefits.limit_text: Full Chinese Government Scholarship covers tuition; Beijing Government Scholarship and the Tsinghua University Tuition Scholarship cover full or partial tuition for one academic year
benefits.conditions: Depends on the award granted. The Chinese Government Scholarship cannot be combined with tuition scholarships. Tuition rates are in a 2027 tuition list that was not read.

benefits.limit_text: Free university dormitory or an accommodation subsidy under a full Chinese Government Scholarship
benefits.conditions: A partial award covers only some items. Students without it pay: Beijing campus dormitory costs RMB 40 per bed per day (double room) or RMB 30 per bed per day (triple room); housing is allocated online first come, first served.

benefits.limit_text: Stipend under a full Chinese Government Scholarship; amount not stated
benefits.conditions: Depends on the award granted; distribution of the Chinese Government Scholarship may change under higher-authority policy.

benefits.limit_text: Comprehensive medical insurance under a full Chinese Government Scholarship and, usually, the Beijing Government Scholarship
benefits.conditions: Students without it pay accident and hospitalisation insurance of RMB 800 per year.
Paid online when submitting the application; it cannot be paid with the Chinese Government Scholarship. No separate fee for scholarships.
The Tsinghua pages read do not mention international travel costs.

requirements.text: Personal statement written in the online system. Doctoral applicants also upload a brief research experience summary or research plan.

Bachelor's certificate for master's applicants; master's and bachelor's certificates for doctoral applicants. Overseas degrees need CSCSE authentication, mainland degrees CSSD. Expected graduates may send an expected-graduation certificate first, with the degree and authentication before registration.

Undergraduate transcript for master's applicants; undergraduate and graduate transcripts for doctoral applicants. A university GPA certificate is also needed if the transcript does not show the overall GPA. Current students finish the transcript before registration.

HSK or English score report as the programme catalogue requires; HSK results are valid two years. Applicants who studied in Chinese may be exempted with a university certificate and school permission.
requirements.conditional_rule: Scholarship applicants must meet the scholarship's HSK requirement (HSK 4 for Chinese-taught Type B)

requirements.text: Two recommendation letters from associate professors or higher, or senior professionals in the field, submitted online or as signed letters. For direct doctorate entry the letters must say the applicant can pursue a doctorate directly.
Bio page of an ordinary passport; holders of a diplomatic visa in China also submit that visa page.
Nationality status documents according to the 2027 nationality submission instructions, delivered by the stated deadline.
Additional documents required by some programmes (see 'Remarks of Application' in the catalogue).
Foreigner Physical Examination Form covering all listed items, with physician's signature, hospital stamp and sealed photo, valid 6 months.
requirements.conditional_rule: Chinese Government Scholarship applicants (and for the visa)

requirements.text: Non-criminal record report usually issued within 6 months before submission; a commitment letter replaces it only where the country issues no such report.
Scans in colour of originals (no phone photos or scans of copies), in Chinese or English or with a notarised translation submitted with the original. Uploaded documents are not returned.

application_steps.title: Check the 2027 catalogue and prepare documents
application_steps.detail: Choose a programme in the 2027 Catalogue of Doctoral and Master's Programmes for International Students and read its 'Remarks of Application' for deadlines, language level and extra conditions. Prepare scans early: the winter break runs 21 January to 17 February 2027, so verification can be slow and the office advises applying 2 to 3 weeks early.

application_steps.title: Apply online and pay the fee
application_steps.detail: Use Tsinghua's online application portal for international applicants, which was expected to open from mid-September 2026 to February 2027. Fill in the form, upload the documents and pay the RMB 800 fee at submission; unpaid or incomplete applications are not processed. You may name up to two programme preferences: submit the first, and the second opens automatically only if the first is not admitted. Schwarzman Scholars and MBA applicants use separate sites.

application_steps.title: Apply by mid-December 2026 if you want the Chinese Government Scholarship
application_steps.detail: To be considered for the Chinese Government Scholarship, finish the online graduate application by the mid-December 2026 first-round deadline. Type B is only for pre-admitted applicants recommended by their school or department. When the school informs you, complete the application in the CSC system and download it; failing to reply or to finish on time counts as withdrawal. Tuition scholarships need no separate form: your scholarship intention in the application counts.

application_steps.title: Document review and comprehensive assessment
application_steps.detail: Expert groups from the school or department review the documents and pick candidates for a comprehensive assessment, generally an interview. Format and timing are set by each school or department and sent to candidates. Applicants for direct doctorate entry usually take a public interview.

application_steps.title: Admission list and scholarship decisions
application_steps.detail: Tsinghua weighs the document review, the assessment and other factors to set the admission list; status can be checked in the application system. For Type B, Tsinghua selects from pre-admitted students recommended by departments and nominates them to the China Scholarship Council, which has experts check eligibility and academic performance and shortlists candidates. Type B results usually come in July to August; tuition scholarship results usually come between June and August, shown in the appendix to the admission notice.

application_steps.title: Receive the Admission Notice and apply for a visa
application_steps.detail: After results Tsinghua issues the Certificate of Admission with an appendix. Students apply for an X1 student visa at a Chinese embassy or consulate with an ordinary passport, the admission notice and appendix, the JW201/JW202 form and a foreigner physical examination record. Names must match the passport used for the application.

application_steps.title: Register and keep the scholarship through the annual review
application_steps.detail: Enter China on the X1 visa and apply for a residence permit within 30 days. Registration is normally in late August or early September, with original degree certificates and the university's designated authentication; failing this review means disqualification. Every Chinese Government Scholarship holder must pass an annual review of academic performance, attitude, attendance, conduct and rewards or punishments, or the scholarship is suspended or ended.
